# SimPO Objective

SimPO (Meng, Xia & Chen, 2024) minimizes:

$$
\mathcal{L}_{\text{SimPO}}(\pi_\theta) = -\,\mathbb{E}_{(x, y_w, y_l)\sim\mathcal{D}}\left[\log \sigma\!\left(\frac{\beta}{|y_w|}\log \pi_\theta(y_w \mid x) \;-\; \frac{\beta}{|y_l|}\log \pi_\theta(y_l \mid x) \;-\; \gamma\right)\right]
$$

Its implicit reward is

$$
r_{\text{SimPO}}(x, y) = \frac{\beta}{|y|}\log \pi_\theta(y \mid x) = \frac{\beta}{|y|}\sum_{i=1}^{|y|}\log \pi_\theta(y_i \mid x, y_{<i})
$$

DPO's reward, for comparison, is

$$
r_{\text{DPO}}(x, y) = \beta \log \frac{\pi_\theta(y \mid x)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y \mid x)}
$$

## Two differences from DPO's reward

1. **No reference model.** SimPO drops $\pi_{\text{ref}}$ entirely. The reward depends only on the policy's own likelihood. This aligns the training reward with the quantity used at generation time, and it saves the memory and compute of running a reference model.

2. **Length normalization.** SimPO divides the log-likelihood by the response length $|y|$, so the reward is an average per-token log-probability rather than a summed one. This removes the bias toward longer responses that a summed log-probability can introduce.

The paper also adds a **target reward margin** $\gamma > 0$ inside the Bradley–Terry term. It requires the winning response's reward to exceed the losing one's by at least $\gamma$. This is part of the objective rather than the reward itself. Some summaries list the two key changes as (1) the length-normalized, reference-free reward and (2) the margin $\gamma$.
